The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel mechanism of action for BRAF inhibitors, which is the ability to modulate mitochondrial metabolism in BRAF mutant cells.

we have shown that inhibition of BRAF mutant signaling by a specific inhibitor, vemurafenib in this study, results in a metabolic shift from glycolysis to oxidative phosphorylation and anaplerosis, and that the magnitude of the metabolic shift is correlated with the degree of BRAF signaling activity in the cell.

BRAF mutant melanoma cells exhibit a metabolic phenotype that is different from BRAF wild-type cells and that BRAF inhibition leads to a metabolic switch that may be exploited therapeutically and as a potential imaging marker.
